headline: Futures Steady as Bonds and Stocks Find Footing; Software Pressure, Biotech Strength Set the Tone
body_html:
Markets head into Thursday's open on constructive footing after Wednesday's session delivered a broad advance, with 345 of 545 names in our universe finishing higher. Equities and bonds gained in tandem as investors positioned ahead of fresh U.S. economic data and scheduled Federal Reserve commentary — a combination that also drove the yen sharply higher against the dollar and nudged Treasury yields lower.

Wednesday's sector scorecard showed Materials leading the tape with a 1.17% gain, followed closely by Healthcare at 1.09% and Energy at 0.98%. Semiconductors and Consumer names also contributed, while Industrials barely registered. The lone laggard was Software, which shed 0.88% as a cluster of high-profile names absorbed heavy selling pressure following earnings-driven disappointments.

For Thursday, the key catalysts to monitor are incoming U.S. macro data and any guidance from Fed officials — the twin forces that animated Wednesday's rally. Middle East tensions have pushed oil to fresh six-week highs, adding an inflationary variable that the bond market will need to digest. Watch the open for follow-through in Materials and Healthcare, and whether Software can stabilize after Wednesday's bruising.

briefs.headline: Biotech Leads Wednesday's Winners as Two Names Surge Above 8%
briefs.body: Sarepta Therapeutics jumped 8.81% and Alnylam rose 8.65% on Wednesday, powering Healthcare to the second-best sector return of the session. The paired move suggests broad-based buying in the biotech corridor rather than a single catalyst, and traders will watch whether the momentum carries into Thursday's open.

briefs.headline: Software Sector Takes the Hardest Hit; Database and Cybersecurity Names Lead Decline
briefs.body: Software was the only sector in the red on Wednesday, falling 0.88%. MongoDB tumbled 13.54%, Palo Alto Networks dropped 9.28%, and Datadog shed 6.53%, pointing to earnings-related de-rating across the group. Sprinklr and Samsara added to the pressure, leaving the sector nursing its worst single-session performance in the current run.

briefs.headline: Oil Touches Six-Week Peak as Middle East Flashpoint Intensifies
briefs.body: Crude prices climbed to their highest level in six weeks on Wednesday as the standoff over a contested ridge in southern Lebanon between Israeli and Hezbollah forces drew fresh international warnings, including from Iran. Energy stocks reflected the move, with the sector gaining 0.98% — one of the better performances of the day.

briefs.headline: Credo Technology Plunges More Than 20%, Steepest Drop in Universe
briefs.body: Connectivity chipmaker Credo Technology was Wednesday's hardest-hit name, skidding 20.04% in the sharpest single-session decline across our 545-name universe. The selloff dragged on the broader Semiconductors sector even as that group managed a net gain of 0.91%, suggesting resilience elsewhere in the chip space.

briefs.headline: Fed Remarks and U.S. Data in Focus as Thursday's Catalysts Take Shape
briefs.body: Scheduled Federal Reserve commentary and a fresh round of U.S. economic releases are the primary events that traders will track on Thursday. Wednesday's rally was explicitly tied to anticipation of those data points; any upside or downside surprise could quickly reprice the rates-sensitive corners of the market that benefited most overnight.

briefs.headline: India Services Activity Picks Up in August but Remains Near Multi-Year Low
briefs.body: India's services sector grew at a faster clip in August compared with the prior month, though the latest PMI reading still hovers near its weakest level in roughly four years. The data adds nuance to the emerging-market growth picture and may weigh on sentiment toward Asia-exposed consumer and industrial names at the open.
